Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires have made their way to the middle followed by the players of West Indies Women Under-19. Trisha Hardat will bowl the first over of the chase. Fahomida Choya and Juairiya Ferdous will open the inning for Bangladesh Women Under-19.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Nishita Akter Nishi is up for a chat after her brilliant performance with the ball. She says that the conditions are favorable for the bowlers as the ball is gripping off the surface. Further adds that her captain has a lot of faith in her bowling and she likes to deliver for her team. In the end says that they have a good batting line up and it will be a good chase for them.

With a modest target of 55 runs to chase, the Bangladesh Women Under-19 team will be confident of securing a comfortable victory. The West Indies, on the other hand, will need to produce a remarkable bowling display and pick quick wickets. Which side will come out on top? We shall find out soon. Chase coming up shortly...

Nishita Akter Nishi was the standout performer for the Bangladeshi side, claiming 3 crucial wickets to peg back the West Indies innings. Her impressive spell was ably supported by the rest of the bowling unit, who collectively stifled the West Indies batting lineup. It was a brilliant day for Bangladesh on the field as well as they have managed to concede just 54 runs in 13 overs.

The Bangladesh Women Under-19 team has delivered an outstanding bowling performance, restricting the West Indies Women Under-19 side to a paltry 54 runs in a rain-curtailed 13-over contest. The Bangladeshi bowlers were relentless in their pursuit of wickets, striking at regular intervals to deny the West Indies any semblance of control.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! A rain-reduced game of 13 overs per side is about to start as the players and the umpires walk out to the middle and take the field. The pair of Asabi Callender and Samara Ramnath will open the batting for West Indies Women Under-19. Nishita Akter Nishi has the new ball in hand for Bangladesh Women Under-19. Let's Play!
The Match officials and the players walk out to the ground in straight lines for the National Anthems. It is the National Anthem of the West Indies followed by that of Bangladesh.

Bangladesh Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Fahomida Choya, Mst Sumaiya Akther Suborna, Juairiya Ferdous, Sumaiya Akter (C), Afia Ashima Era, Jannatul Maoua, Sadia Islam, Mst Farjana Easmin, Habiba Islam Pinky, Nishita Akter Nishi, Mst Anisa Akter Soba.

West Indies Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Asabi Callender, Samara Ramnath (C), Naijanni Cumberbatch, Jahzara Claxton, Brianna Harricharan, Abigail Bryce, Amrita Ramtahal, Aaliyah Weekes, Denella Creese, Erin Deane, Trisha Hardat.

The captain of West Indies Women Under-19, Samara Ramnath says that they were looking to have a bowl first as well but they will be now looking to bat first and put up a good score on the board. The overs are reduced to 13 overs and it is important for them to have a good start with the bat, says Samara.

The skipper of Bangladesh Women Under-19, Sumaiya Akter says that they will want to bowl first as the conditions are favourable for the bowlers and they will look to take advantage of that. She says that the tournament has made them learn alot and they will look to play a good brand of cricket in their final game of the tournament.
TOSS - Bangladesh Women Under-19 have won the toss and elected to have a BOWL first. It is going to be a 13 over per side game.

The West Indies team, on the other hand, has had a mixed tournament so far. Despite having some talented players in their ranks, they have struggled to find consistency. Led by their captain, Samara Ramnath, the team will be looking to perform strongly to keep their semifinal hopes alive. Windies have entered the Super Six stage with no points under their belt as they did not defeat any time that has advanced to the Super Six in their group games.

The Bangladesh team has made a promising start to the tournament, delivering impressive performances in the group stage. Under the leadership of captain Sumaiya Akter, the team has showcased a well-rounded performance, boasting a balanced mix of batting, bowling, and fielding prowess. The bowling trio of Anisa Akter Soba, Jannatul Maoua, and Nishita Akter Nishi has been instrumental in picking up crucial wickets, while captain Sumaiya Akter and Afia Ashima Era have led the batting charge. Notably, despite losing, the team pushed the formidable Australian side hard, restricting them to a precarious position by claiming 8 wickets. Although they didn't emerge victorious, this spirited display would have significantly boosted the team's confidence and morale.

The ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025, has reached its business end, with the Super Six stage underway. In Match 8, Bangladesh Women Under-19 will take on West Indies Women Under-19 in a crucial encounter that could have significant implications for both teams' semifinal hopes.

The ICC Women’s Under-19 World Cup 2025 has entered the high-stakes Super Six stage, and this clash between West Indies Women Under-19 and Bangladesh Women Under-19 promises plenty of drama! The Windies are battling for pride after a tough tournament. With just one win so far, their batting struggles have been glaring, especially after being bowled out for a meager 53 in their first Super Six game - their third sub-100 total in just four matches. But don’t count them out! Skipper Samara Ramnath will be determined to lead from the front with the bat and ball, while Asabi Callender, Jahzara Claxton, and Abigail Bryce will look to deliver in key moments. In the bowling department, Ramnath’s accurate off-breaks, combined with the spin support from Naijanni Cumberbatch and Erin Deane, will be pivotal. Selena Ross and Claxton will also shoulder the pace attack. They may be out of the semifinal race, but the Windies are playing for pride and could spoil their opponent's dreams. For Bangladesh Women Under-19, this match is all about keeping their semifinal hopes alive. With a crucial game against India before this, a win in both matches guarantees their spot in the semis. However, one slip-up could leave them relying on other results. Their bowling attack has been their biggest weapon, with the spin duo of Mst Anisa Akter Soba and Jannatul Maoua wreaking havoc in the tournament. The way they pushed Australia to the brink while defending a modest total speaks volumes about their skill and determination. On the batting front, skipper Sumaiya Akter holds the key to their fortunes. She’ll need support from Afia Ashima Era, Juairiya Ferdous, and Fahomida Choya to put up a fighting total or chase down targets under pressure. It’s a clash of pride versus ambition. Can the Windies bounce back and finish on a high, or will the Tigresses roar loud? Buckle up - it’s going to be a cracker!
